scope: EVM settlement path (x402 settler and its callers), ops emergency controls, browser extension message boundary, Elements/Liquid exposure

sources_searched.Savant: no report found in the repository
sources_searched.CertiK: no FurlPay report found in the repository (CertiK's public Liquid incident analysis is an external reference, not a FurlPay audit)

severity_scale: P0 critical, P1 high, P2 medium, P3 low, P4 informational, PN needs validation

findings.title: Ops rail/global pause not enforced at the irreversible settlement boundary
findings.description: assertRailActive() is called only at the top of some routes. The public facilitator settle route, account funding, the x402 paywall and MPP reach defaultSettler() without any pause check, and a request that passed a route-top check before a pause landed still settles (TOCTOU). An operator pausing in an incident would believe broadcasting had stopped when it had not.
findings.preconditions: On-chain settlement live (ONCHAIN_SETTLEMENT_LIVE on, KMS configured) and an incident in progress.
findings.evidence: grep of assertRailActive callers, 2026-10-03; facilitator/settle/route.ts has no pause check.
findings.rationale_for_severity: Bypass of a secondary safeguard (containment control). Not P1: production settlement is gated off by ONCHAIN_SETTLEMENT_LIVE/KMS today, and the bypass needs an incident to matter.
findings.remediation: Settlement safety gate inside the settler (beforeBroadcast) checking the durable breaker AND the ops global pause, failing closed.
findings.regression_test: settlementSafety.spec.ts: 'the ops console's global pause stops the settler', '10/11 halt raised mid-flight'
findings.retest: 30/30 safety spec pass; residual: rail-scope pauses remain route-level by design (settler cannot tell which rail called it)
findings.residual_risk: Rail-scope pause still does not stop the facilitator route; use a network or global halt.

findings.title: Emergency control state fails open on store read errors
findings.description: controls.ts deliberately does not fail closed when Redis cannot be read. Correct for quotes; wrong for broadcasts.
findings.preconditions: Redis outage during an active pause.
findings.evidence: Module header comment and readFlag implementation.
findings.remediation: Settler-side gate fails closed on any read error (state, epoch, ops pause, velocity counter).
findings.status: fixed for the settlement path (pending deploy); route-level behaviour unchanged by design
findings.regression_test: settlementSafety.spec.ts: '20. an unreadable control plane refuses settlement'
findings.residual_risk: Quote routes still fail open on a control-plane outage (intended).

findings.title: RPC chain identity not verified before signing with local/KMS accounts
findings.description: viem asserts the RPC's chain id only for json-rpc accounts. For local and KMS accounts it signs for the configured chain and then trusts receipts from whatever the RPC is. A misconfigured or wrong-network RPC would have its receipts treated as settlement evidence.
findings.evidence: node_modules/viem/_esm/actions/wallet/sendTransaction.js: assertCurrentChain only in the json-rpc branch.
findings.validation: confirmed by reading the library source
findings.remediation: Probe eth_chainId on every configured provider before signing; mismatch halts the network.
findings.regression_test: settlementSafety.spec.ts: '2. a wrong chain id refuses the request and halts the network'
findings.residual_risk: A provider that lies consistently about everything is not detectable with one provider (FP-SET-06).

findings.title: Settlement success relied on receipt status alone
findings.description: A `success` receipt was reported as settled without checking that it contained exactly the authorized Transfer and AuthorizationUsed events. Exploitation requires the pinned token contract to misbehave (upgrade) or the RPC to serve a different receipt.
findings.preconditions: Token contract upgrade or lying RPC.
findings.remediation: verifySettlementReceipt; mismatch halts the network and surfaces as SettlementPendingError so every caller records the tx unresolved.

findings.title: No per-network index of unresolved settlements; no reorg re-check of confirmed ones
findings.description: Settlement records were keyed only by tx hash, so nothing could enumerate pending/abandoned settlements or re-check recent confirmations for reorgs.
findings.remediation: Sorted-set indexes maintained in recordSettlement; reconcileNetwork() pass; recovery blocked while any are unresolved.
findings.status: fixed (pending deploy); reconciler not yet scheduled
findings.residual_risk: Reconciler runs only on recovery actions until wired to a cron (founder/ops decision). Records written before the index existed are not indexed.

findings.title: Single-RPC deployments cannot detect provider disagreement
findings.description: With one provider, a consistently lying or forked RPC is undetectable. Whether production has a fallback configured could not be verified from the repository.
findings.preconditions: Only one RPC configured for a settlement network.
findings.validation: awaiting validation: list production env var names (not values) for *_RPC_URL_FALLBACK
findings.remediation: Configure an independent second provider per settlement network. The probe reports `rpc_unverified` until then.
findings.regression_test: settlementSafety.spec.ts: 'a single provider is reported as unverified'

findings.title: No detection of USDC proxy implementation changes
findings.description: The allowlist pins token addresses but not their implementation. FP-SET-04's receipt check covers misbehaviour after an upgrade; watching the FiatToken proxy Upgraded event would give earlier warning.
findings.remediation: Watch the proxy implementation slot / Upgraded events; halt on change pending review.
findings.residual_risk: Covered after the fact by FP-SET-04.

findings.title: Gasless transfers record pending outcomes outside the settlement store
findings.description: On SettlementPendingError the gasless route writes a tx event (recordTxEvent) but not a SettlementRecord, so the reconciler and the recovery gate do not see its unresolved transactions.
findings.remediation: Also call recordSettlement with status pending in that branch.
findings.residual_risk: A disputed gasless tx would not block recovery.

findings.title: Single admin identity makes dual-approval recovery impossible
findings.description: Critical incidents require two distinct approvers; only one account can hold the admin role. Critical halts therefore cannot be resumed. This fails closed; it is an operational constraint, not a vulnerability.
findings.remediation: Founder decision: add a second admin identity, or explicitly accept single-operator recovery (not implemented).
findings.regression_test: settlementSafety.spec.ts: '15. a critical incident needs two distinct approvers'
findings.residual_risk: Operational lock-out after a critical incident.

findings.title: Ops resume of a rail/global pause is single-operator with no step-up
findings.description: Resuming a paused rail needs only the admin role and an 8-character reason. No step-up, no second approver. The new settlement breaker has both; the older controls do not.
findings.remediation: Require recentStepUp on resume; consider routing resume through the breaker's approval workflow.
findings.residual_risk: A hijacked admin session can resume a paused rail (but cannot clear a breaker halt).

findings.title: Extension service worker trusted all same-id senders, including content scripts
findings.description: Content scripts on every HTTPS page share the extension id; only a static source test kept them from privileged handlers (REVOKE_PASSKEY, LOGOUT, STEP_UP_*, DECLINE_CHALLENGE, RAMP_CHECKOUT). A compromised renderer is not bound by source.
findings.preconditions: Renderer compromise on any open page.
findings.status: fixed (committed d138658; extension not yet published)

findings.title: Elements rangeproof-cache consensus bug (Liquid incident 2026-09-06): FurlPay exposure
findings.source: external advisory: Blockstream incident assessment; CertiK incident analysis
findings.description: Upstream: Elements v0.14.1 to v23.3.3 cached rangeproof/surjection-proof validation under an ambiguous key, allowing unbacked L-BTC issuance; fixed in v23.3.4 (2026-09-09). No CVE ID stated by Blockstream. FurlPay runs no Elements node and has no Liquid asset in any settlement, signing or ledger path; its only Liquid touchpoint is a read-only intel feed whose peg-out observations during the incident window included unbacked flows.
findings.confidence: high for the repository; unknown for partners
findings.validation: repository verified; partner L-BTC acceptance unknown
findings.remediation: None in code. Confirm no partner or treasury counterparty accepts L-BTC on FurlPay's behalf.
findings.residual_risk: Counterparty exposure, if any, is outside FurlPay's control.
